        "# Week 1: Cleaning the Applicant Dataset By Maryam Sheraz"
      ],

      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "import pandas as pd\n",
        "import random\n",
        "random.seed(1)"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "O2mU2OdYmi_C"
      },
      "execution_count": 69,
      "outputs": []
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "names = [\"Ali Khan\", \"Sara Ahmed\", \"Hina Malik\", \"Usman Tariq\", \"Ayesha Noor\", \"Bilal Raza\"]\n",
        "domains = [\"web dev\", \"Web Development\", \"WEB DEV\", \"data science\", \"Data Science\", \"DATA SCIENCE\",\n",
        "           \"ai/ml\", \"AI/ML\", \"app dev\", \"App Development\", \"graphic design\", \"Graphic Design\"]\n",
        "universities = [\"NUST\", \"nust\", \"FAST\", \"UET\", \"PU\", \"Punjab University\"]\n",
        "statuses = [\"Under Review\", \"Selected\", \"Rejected\", \"selected\", \"REJECTED\"]\n",
        "dates = [\"12/05/2026\", \"2026-05-12\", \"03/06/2026\", \"2026-06-20\"]\n",
        "\n",
        "rows = []\n",
        "for i in range(80):\n",
        "    rows.append({\n",
        "        \"Applicant Name\": random.choice(names),\n",
        "        \"Email\": \"student\" + str(i) + \"@example.com\",\n",
        "        \"Phone\": \"0300-\" + str(random.randint(1000000, 9999999)),\n",
        "        \"Domain Applied\": random.choice(domains),\n",
        "        \"University\": random.choice(universities),\n",
        "        \"Application Date\": random.choice(dates),\n",
        "        \"Status\": random.choice(statuses),\n",
        "    })\n",
        "\n",
        "df = pd.DataFrame(rows)\n",
        "df.head()"
      ],

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Step 3: First Look at the Data The dataset has 84 rows and 7 columns. Applicant Name, Email, University and Status each have 2 missing values. There are 3 rows that are exactly the same. The Application Date column is stored as text, not as a real date."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "JLXwTMHeoQ-j"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "df = df.dropna(subset=[\"Applicant Name\"])\n",
        "df = df.dropna(subset=[\"Email\"])\n",
        "df[\"University\"] = df[\"University\"].fillna(\"Not Specified\")\n",
        "df[\"Status\"] = df[\"Status\"].fillna(\"Under Review\")"
      ],

      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Step 4: Handling Missing Values\n",
        "\n",
        "I removed the rows with a missing Applicant Name, because an application without a name cannot be used. I also removed the rows with a missing Email, because we need the email to contact the applicant.\n",
        "\n",
        "I filled the missing University values with \"Not Specified\", because this information is not very important.\n",
        "\n",
        "I filled the missing Status values with \"Under Review\", because it probably means the application has not been checked yet."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "m7RnVv8rpRhN"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "df = df.drop_duplicates()\n",

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Step 5: Removing Duplicates\n",
        "\n",
        "I found 3 rows that were exactly the same and removed them. Then I made all emails lowercase and removed 1 more row that had the same email as another row, but with the name written in capital letters.\n",
        "\n",
        "I checked duplicates by email because a person can write their name in different ways, but their email stays the same. So email is a more reliable way to find the same person."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "y1q4nJbXqDKM"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "df[\"Applicant Name\"] = df[\"Applicant Name\"].str.strip().str.title()\n",
        "df[\"Status\"] = df[\"Status\"].str.strip().str.title()"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "1nuk4yWSp-Xc"
      },
      "execution_count": 83,
      "outputs": []
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "df[\"Domain Applied\"] = df[\"Domain Applied\"].str.strip().str.lower()\n",
        "\n",
        "domain_fix = {\n",
        "    \"web dev\": \"Web Development\",\n",
        "    \"web development\": \"Web Development\",\n",
        "    \"data science\": \"Data Science\",\n",
        "    \"ai/ml\": \"AI/ML\",\n",
        "    \"app dev\": \"App Development\",\n",
        "    \"app development\": \"App Development\",\n",
        "    \"graphic design\": \"Graphic Design\"\n",
        "}\n",
        "\n",
        "df[\"Domain Applied\"] = df[\"Domain Applied\"].map(domain_fix)\n",
        "df[\"Domain Applied\"].unique()"
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "colab": {

        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "code",
      "source": [
        "df[\"University\"] = df[\"University\"].str.strip().str.lower()\n",
        "\n",
        "uni_fix = {\n",
        "    \"nust\": \"NUST\",\n",
        "    \"fast\": \"FAST\",\n",
        "    \"uet\": \"UET\",\n",

        "\n",
        "df[\"University\"] = df[\"University\"].map(uni_fix)\n",
        "df[\"University\"].unique()\n"

      "source": [
        "## Step 6: Standardizing Text\n",
        "\n",
        "The same value was written in different ways, for example \"web dev\" and \"WEB DEV\". The computer sees these as different values, so counts would be wrong.\n",
        "\n",
        "I removed extra spaces and made the casing the same. Then I mapped all the different spellings of Domain Applied to 5 clean names. I did the same for University and Status."
      ],

      }
    },

    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Step 7: Fixing Data Types\n",
        "\n",
        "The Application Date column was stored as text, so it could not be sorted or used for calculations. I converted it to a real date type. I used errors=\"coerce\" so that any unreadable date would become empty instead of crashing the notebook. After the conversion, there were 0 empty dates.\n",
        "\n",
        "The Phone column had dashes and spaces in different places. I removed them to make the format the same. I kept Phone as text so the leading zero does not disappear."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "B6Wb7LMCsgRM"
      }
    },
    {
      "cell_type": "markdown",
      "source": [
        "## Data Quality Summary\n",
        "\n",
        "**Starting data:** 84 rows and 7 columns.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Problems I found:**\n",
        "- Some cells were empty: 2 names, 2 emails, 2 universities and 2 statuses.\n",
        "- Some rows were repeated: 3 were exactly the same, and 1 more had the same email as another row.\n",
        "- The same domain was written in many ways. There were 12 different spellings for only 5 real domains.\n",
        "- University and Status were also written in different ways, like \"nust\" and \"NUST\".\n",
        "- Application Date was saved as text, not as a real date.\n",
        "- Phone numbers had dashes and spaces.\n",
        "\n",
        "**What I did to fix them:**\n",
        "- I removed the 2 rows with no name, because we cannot use an application without a name.\n",
        "- I removed the 2 rows with no email, because we need the email to contact the person.\n",
        "- I wrote \"Not Specified\" in the empty University cells, because it is not very important.\n",
        "- I wrote \"Under Review\" in the empty Status cells, because the application was probably not checked yet.\n",
        "- I removed 4 repeated rows in total: 3 exact copies and 1 with the same email.\n",
        "- I made the spellings the same. Now there are only 5 domains and 3 statuses.\n",
        "- I changed Application Date into a real date.\n",
        "- I removed the dashes and spaces from the phone numbers.\n",
        "\n",
        "**Final data:** 76 rows and 7 columns. There are no empty cells, no repeated rows, and all the text looks the same ."
      ],
      "metadata": {
        "id": "wBTi0mxtt1dL"
      }
    },

        "status_by_domain = pd.pivot_table(\n",

        "print(status_by_domain)\n",
        "\n",
        "status_by_domain_pct = status_by_domain.div(status_by_domain.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 100\n",
        "print(status_by_domain_pct.round(1))"
